subject: Service commitments, measurement windows, and customer metrics access - procurement questionnaire (Acme)
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@acme.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: service commitments, measurement & evidence

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is our standard procurement questionnaire (acme_procurement_questions.xlsx) — a few items are specific to service-level commitments and monitoring and I'd appreciate concise answers so our procurement and SRE teams can sign off. High level questions we need covered: 

- How does Redwood define "uptime" for hosted endpoints? Is it per-region, per-model, or per-deployment? What rolling window(s) are used to compute availability?
- Which latency metrics do you publish (p50/p95/p99)? Over what aggregation window and sampling approach? Do you measure end-to-end latency (ingress → final token) or server-side only?
- How are errors and timeouts classified (5xx, model timeouts, throttles)? What counts as an SLA breach?
- For notifications: do customers get alerted for SLO breaches or only post-incident reports? Can we subscribe to alerts?
- Can customers access raw metrics (Prometheus endpoint / read-only dashboard) or do you only provide periodic reports?
- What exception policies exist for planned maintenance, model rollouts, or emergency mitigations (are there blackout windows that do not count against SLA)?

Our procurement team would like concrete examples (e.g., "Availability is measured per endpoint over a 30-day rolling window with 99.95% target; availability is computed as successful requests / total requests excluding scheduled maintenance windows"), and any sample dashboards or export formats you can share.

Would it be possible to have a short call with someone from your platform/ops team if needed? We're trying to finish evaluation by 01/22.

Thanks,
Elena Martin
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

----

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: service commitments, measurement & evidence

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and the deadline. I've answered the items below at a procurement level; I attached a short operational definitions doc (Redwood_SLO_Operational_Definitions.pdf) with examples and wording you can paste into your template. If you want a deeper technical call we can loop in Platform/Infra.

Quick answers (summary):
- Uptime (availability): measured per deployment (customer endpoint) and per-region for hosted; target and measurement window are configurable per contract but our standard for hosted API is 99.95% over a 30-day rolling window. Availability = successful 2xx responses / total requests, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and customer-requested private maintenance.

- Latency metrics: we publish p50, p95, and p99 server-side latency (time from request received by our edge to final token emitted). For hosted customers we also provide end-to-end estimates that include network tail latency in shared-region reports. Aggregation is via rolling windows (1m, 5m, 30m) and then computed into daily/30-day summaries for SLO evaluation.

- Errors/timeouts: classified as 5xx server errors, model timeouts (internal runtime exceeding configured token/time limits), and throttles (rate-limits). SLA breach is triggered by availability falling below the agreed SLO in the contract after excluding maintenance windows and agreed exceptions. See doc for exact formula and examples.

- Alerts & notifications: customers can subscribe to real-time alerts (webhook or email) for error-rate spikes and SLO-threshold crossings. For hosted contracts we offer a read-only dashboard with historical metrics and an automated weekly SLO report. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide direct metrics export and tighter integrations.

- Metrics access: Hosted customers receive aggregated dashboards and periodic exports (CSV/API). For Dedicated and Private deployments we provide a read-only Prometheus endpoint and can enable a Grafana read-only dashboard on request (subject to contractual controls). We cannot expose per-tenant raw traces from our shared-hosted pool for multi-tenant privacy reasons.

- Exceptions and maintenance: Planned maintenance windows (announced 72+ hours in advance) do not count against SLA. Emergency mitigations (e.g., model rollback for safety) are handled case-by-case; our standard contract includes an exceptions clause — we will provide a post-incident report and, if appropriate, a pro-rated credit per the SLA.

Next steps: I can share the hosted sample dashboard link and a short, redlined paragraph you can drop into your questionnaire. Do you want us to provide a read-only Grafana link (Dedicated) or a hosted SLO report sample (Hosted)?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: service commitments, measurement & evidence

Lauren — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups from our SRE and security teams: 

- For Dedicated deployment options: can you confirm Prometheus exposition format and whether we can scrape metrics on a standard interval? We'd prefer pull (scrape) with basic auth / mTLS rather than you pushing metrics into our environment.
- For Hosted: you said aggregated dashboards — can you share a sample dashboard URL and an example CSV export of a 30-day SLO report?
- For model rollouts: when you say "exceptions are case-by-case", can you provide an example of a recent rollout where a temporary SLA exception was declared and how it was communicated?

If possible, can Platform/Infra join a 30-minute call early next week (our slot: Tue 01/19 10:00-11:00 PT)? I'm attaching our security contact list for scheduling.

Thanks — Elena

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Procurement questionnaire: service commitments, measurement & evidence

Karthik — forwarding Acme's follow-ups from procurement/SRE. They want to scrape Prometheus for Dedicated and a sample hosted SLO CSV + an example of a rollout exception. Quick summary and ask:

- Can we approve providing a read-only Prometheus endpoint (scrape) for Dedicated customers behind mTLS/basic auth? This would be a new offering but aligns with our Dedicated value prop. Security will still need to sign off, and we should require a data-processing appendix.
- For Hosted: can Platform produce a 30-day sample SLO CSV export and a hosted dashboard link that doesn't expose tenant-level traces?
- Do we have a sanitized example of a recent model rollout that triggered an exception (timelines, mitigation, communication) that we can share as an anonymized post-incident example?

Proposed reply to Acme (draft):
"We can enable a read-only Prometheus endpoint for Dedicated customers behind mTLS and provide a sample 30-day SLO CSV and a hosted dashboard link for Hosted customers. Exceptions for rollouts are rare; when they occur we notify customers within 4 hours and follow with a post-incident report within 72 hours. We'll provide an anonymized example of a recent rollout and schedule a 30-minute call with Platform next week."

If you approve, I'll send that and schedule the call for Tue 01/19 10:00 PT. If Security needs to vet the Prometheus approach first, should I route them to our security-eng contact or set a call?

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren — good thread. Approve the proposed reply with two clarifications: 

1) For Dedicated customers, we'll provide a read-only Prometheus scrape endpoint behind mTLS + basic auth, but only after a security review and an executed Data Processing Addendum (DPA). We'll include a short onboarding checklist for network allowlists and cert exchange.

2) For Hosted customers, we will provide aggregated dashboards and a sample 30-day SLO CSV export; we will NOT expose per-request traces from the shared-hosted environment.

Regarding rollout exceptions: share an anonymized post-incident summary (we can redact customer names and replace with "customer X") showing the detection, mitigation (rollback to prior model), and timeline. Confirm we'll provide 72-hour post-incident reports and (for contracted enterprise customers) proactive notification within 4 hours of detection if an SLO may be impacted.

Action: go ahead and send the reply to Acme, attach the sample CSV and dashboard link, and schedule the Tue 01/19 10:00 PT call with Platform. I'll copy Legal if they ask for DPA text.

Thanks — Karthik
